verdict.probe_answer: Both suites trivially 'fail' on pre-change code since the 2-arg signature won't compile. More telling: A's new commit_precedence test only asserts `.0` (the message string), never checking the returned CommitSource, and has zero coverage of the 64KiB bound despite A's own clean_commit_candidate implementing one. B's equivalent test asserts full tuples (message+CommitSource) for every case AND adds an oversize-candidate test (65537 'x' chars) expecting fallback to Title. That test is not trivially passing — it actually fails against Arm A's implementation, which truncates oversized input to 64KiB and returns it as a present Typed message rather than treating it as absent, contradicting the spec's 'mirror read_commit_msg_file's bounding' (whose old contract was None-on-oversize). Strongest A test: commit_precedence_and_comment_only_falls_back_to_title (covers 4 precedence branches). Weakest A test: same one, for omitting `.1` checks and the oversize case. Strongest B test: the oversize-boundary case in the same-named test — a real edge case tied to spec intent. Weakest B test: the retained commit_message_file_else_fallback, fairly mechanical/redundant with the newer test.
verdict.rationale: Functionally both implement typed>file>title>derived precedence correctly for the common paths and update all three call sites plus the warning re-spec. Two concrete differentiators favor B (WRONG-tier, not stylistic): (1) Arm A's clean_commit_candidate truncates an oversized typed/file candidate to 64KiB and uses the truncated text as a present Typed/File message, instead of treating oversize as ABSENT the way read_commit_msg_file's original contract did ('None if absent/unreadable/oversize/...') — a real bug on large inputs, uncaught by A's own tests. Arm B implements and explicitly tests reject-on-oversize. (2) The brief explicitly says '(tweak.rs passes original_message into decide — it does NOT call commit_message; leave it.)' Arm A nonetheless changed decide()'s signature to (String, CommitSource) and modified tweak.rs to satisfy it — a direct violation of an explicit instruction. Arm B kept decide()'s bool-based signature, converting CommitSource to bool only at the commit_message call sites, leaving tweak.rs untouched exactly as instructed. Both compile and are otherwise equivalent in merge.rs handling.
